    People also ask
    What does EASA mean?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    EASA stands for the
    European Union Aviation Safety Agency, the regulatory body responsible for ensuring safety and environmental protection in civil aviation within the EU and associated countries. Headquartered in Cologne, Germany, it sets safety standards, certifies aircraft, and oversees aviation safety regulations. 
    Usage Examples & Functions 
    • Aircraft Certification: EASA certifies new aircraft, such as issuing a type certificate to ensure airworthiness.
    • Safety Regulations: Setting standards for airlines, pilots, and maintenance crews across Europe.
    • Flight Operations:
      Issuing regulations for pilot licensing and commercial air transport.
    • Environmental Standards: Developing rules for noise reduction and emissions.
    • Medical Standards: Establishing requirements for pilot health checks, such as Class 1 medical certificates. 
    Synonyms & Related Terms 
    • European Aviation Safety Agency (original name, still often used).
    • EU Aviation Authority.
    • Regulatory agency/body. 
    Key Details 
    • Members: 27 EU countries + Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, and Norway.
    • Established: 2002.
    • Context: Unlike the US-based FAA (Federal Aviation Administration), EASA operates within the European Economic Area (EEA).
